## Project Setup

This report demonstrates a fully modular Python-based treasury cashflow simulation engine. It generates synthetic daily bank movements, applies internal sweeps, updates balances, and stores results in a SQLite database for downstream analytics and Power BI dashboards.

```{python}

import os
import sys

# Quarto is running inside: .../treasury-cashflow-simulation
# We need to go one level up to reach the repo root
project_root = os.path.dirname(os.getcwd())

# Add shared utilities
utils_path = os.path.join(project_root, "utils")
sys.path.append(utils_path)

# Add project-specific modules
src_path = os.path.join(project_root, "treasury-cashflow-simulation", "src")
sys.path.append(src_path)

print("Python paths configured:")
print(" -", utils_path)
print(" -", src_path)

```

```{python}
from simulate_pipeline import simulate_pipeline
print("simulate_pipeline imported OK")
```

```{python}
import os, stat
```

## Preview Latest Balances

```{python}
import pandas as pd

conn = get_connection()
df_bal = pd.read_sql("""
    SELECT *
    FROM balances
    ORDER BY date DESC
    LIMIT 20
""", conn)
conn.close()

df_bal
```

## Visualise Closing Balances Over Time

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

conn = get_connection()
df = pd.read_sql("""
    SELECT date, account_number, closing_balance
    FROM balances
""", conn)
conn.close()

pivot = df.pivot(index="date", columns="account_number", values="closing_balance")

plt.figure(figsize=(14,6))
pivot.plot()
plt.title("Closing Balances Over Time")
plt.ylabel("Balance")
plt.xlabel("Date")
plt.legend(title="Account Number", bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

```
